Prior review retained below:
Distinct review reread every response against its exact question and checked the 15 briefs/counterevidence. Jetten incumbent and cutoff verified; pending constitutional review, referendums and compulsory military service are excluded. Corrected the firearms circular publication date to 2020-01-31; added dependent-child evidence and actual suspicionless checkpoint evidence. Replaced multilingual-service extrapolation with actual Chinatown street signs. Strengthened essential/infant-industry trade claims with adopted strategic-dependency and open-industrial policy. Replaced generic generative-AI caution with target-population medical-software validation guidance. Withdrew secular-religious-11 and progressive-traditionalist-14 as unsupported comparisons. Culture/Nature uses the actually adopted mandatory Doenvermogen test, not mere public funding of research; professional JGZ guidance is explicitly distinguished from cabinet policy. Six supported causation answers are qualified policy-model inferences, especially generalisation from noncognitive capacity to stress/attention/temperament; parent should scrutinise them. Fourteen nulls remain: culture-nature 02,05,06,07,08,10,11,13,14,15; innovation-caution 08,11; secular-religious 11; progressive-traditionalist 14. Further weaker but explicit inferences for parent review: popular recall absence; migration-capacity tradeoff; public ownership of security-sensitive businesses; redistribution funding and land redistribution; regional tax-competition limits; Indigenous treaty commitments without domestic territories. Sources include primary government, regulators, laws and implemented EU rules crosschecked with AP, NOS, Freedom House, other independent reporting and original research. Commons File page identifies Zscout370 and PD-shape; downloaded 960x640 PNG is 1,077 bytes and visually inspected. No external independent review is claimed, no archive/publication performed. Validation: 14 unresolved null responses prevent archive; no structural/source/image errors after URL deduplication and preserving partial publication dates in titles with date=undated. Neutral warnings on public-private (6/16) and innovation-caution (5/16) were reread: each represents documented mixed ownership or differentiated risk/authorisation rules, not missing evidence. Neighbours are empty because scoring is incomplete. No build or archive was run. Separate completion review: challenged all new estimates against the exact wording and earlier gap reasons. Assumptions remain contextual extrapolations, not verified implemented rules or causal rankings. Specific restrictions: nonsuspect records versus document schedules; public dress versus school accommodations; healthy implanted enhancement versus therapeutic/noninvasive products; interests versus career choices; individual heredity versus national/racial causes; immediate intuition versus reflective education. Neither a modifiable trait nor a funded study proves predominance or adoption. Mixed responses reflect an affirmative interaction or conditional-policy interpretation rather than uncertainty alone. New assumption IDs: secular-religious-11, progressive-traditionalist-14, innovation-caution-08, innovation-caution-11, culture-nature-02, culture-nature-05, culture-nature-06, culture-nature-07, culture-nature-08, culture-nature-10, culture-nature-11, culture-nature-13, culture-nature-14, culture-nature-15. Prior complete same-agent assessment review is retained; this continuation does not claim a fresh independent 240-source reread or human sign-off. Shared credits and validation are recorded in the completion report. Completion validator warnings were read individually: neutral choices reflect mixed ownership, service-specific contracting, staged/graded regulation, family-law distinctions or explicit development interaction. No neighbour reached 95% in the saved pre-archive diagnostics; archive revalidates against added peers.

neutralAnswers.rationale: Educated assumption: Independent courts provide remedies against government administration, but Article 120 blocks constitutional review of primary statutes. The June 2026 proposal to relax that prohibition is not enacted policy. Most likely Neutral. The cited facts provide contextual evidence for an institutional estimate, not a verified explicit national endorsement of this exact statement. Formal constitutional provisions do not alone establish their practical independence or an explicit endorsement of the exact institutional rule.
